subject: Live session throttle: latency spike and recovery advisory
messages:
From: Raj Mehta <raj@fincloud.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: integrations@fincloud.com
Date: Thu, 30 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: High latency on live session streaming since 08:45AM

Hi Stephanie —

We started seeing a sharp increase in tail latency on your streaming/chat endpoint for our live sessions starting ~08:45 ET. Users report long pauses (10-20s) in partial responses, and some streams never complete. This is affecting our in-product chat feature and a few live transcripts were delayed enough to cause user drop-off.

Quick details:
- Endpoint: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate (region: us-east)
- Error/behavior: intermittent chunk delivery pauses, final tokens arriving 8-25s late
- Impact: ~30% of sessions in the last 25 minutes showed at least one pause
- We saw no change on our side; traffic patterns are steady.

Can you confirm if there is an incident on your side and provide ETA / recommended mitigations? We can temporarily fall back to polling-style pulls if that helps.

Attached are a small sample of client-side traces and our dashboard graphs (link inlined). Please escalate — we have a live demo at 10:30 ET.

Thanks,
Raj
Raj Mehta
Head of Integrations, FinCloud
raj@fincloud.com

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 30 Mar 2028 09:24:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: High latency on live session streaming since 08:45AM

Raj — thanks for the quick heads up and the traces, really helpful. I’m escalating immediately and wanted to share short-term mitigations while our on-call engineering team investigates: 

Immediate customer-side mitigations (recommended):
- Switch to polling fallback for critical live flows: reduce perceived latency while we restore streaming.
- If you can, reduce the model max_tokens for live sessions and lower the chunk size to 64 tokens to reduce per-chunk processing.
- Implement a client reconnect and resume strategy (keep last event id) to tolerate brief stalls.

What we’re doing now (on our side):
- Triage on-call is looking at edge queue metrics and batching windows; we’ve flagged auto-scaler and recent edge router changes.
- I’ve requested a prioritized trace dump and log bundle — please see attachment request (small log snippets are useful).
- We’ll open an incident and keep you updated every 30–60 minutes until resolved.

We’ll also offer a goodwill credit depending on impact. I’ll send a remediation note and recommended SDK settings within the hour.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.com
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0192

Date: Thu, 30 Mar 2028 14:05:00 -04:00
Subject: RE: High latency on live session streaming since 08:45AM — incident summary and next steps

Raj — apologies again for the disruption this morning. I’m writing with a short summary of what happened, what we changed, and recommended actions for your team.

Summary / Root cause (short):
- At ~08:30 ET a configuration change to the edge batching window rolled out to a subset of us-east edge routers; the effective batching window increased from 20ms to ~80ms in some clusters. This caused increased per-request queuing and larger batch sizes which amplified tail latency for streaming requests. The change also interacted poorly with a recent autoscaler tuning (slower scale-up), so queues grew and some streams experienced long pause events.

What we did:
- Identified the configuration drift and rolled back the batching-window change at ~10:05 ET.
- Deployed a hotfix to autoscaler thresholds to reduce scale-up latency and avoid oscillation.
- Flushed KV caches for affected routers and restarted a small set of edge workers to drain backlogs.
- Monitored for continued anomalies; by ~11:20 ET streaming latencies returned to normal baselines.

Customer impact & credits:
- Impact window: 08:30–11:20 ET; we estimate ~27% of live sessions in that window saw at least one pause.
- We will apply a 10% service credit for usage during the impacted window; our billing team will follow up.

Short-term recommendations for FinCloud (client):
- If you need absolute resilience during live demos, enable polling fallback for mission-critical flows.
- Set client-side stream keepalives (5s) and implement reconnect/resume logic (we can share a small snippet).
- Consider pinning to a lower-latency model variant for live sessions during peak periods — we can suggest variants that trade a small accuracy delta for lower latency.

Next steps & follow-up:
- We will publish a full postmortem (root cause, timeline, remediation, and preventive actions) by EOD tomorrow and share a link.
- Action items assigned: INC-1724 will track the autoscaler and rollout controls work (owner: Karthik).
- I’ve attached the interim postmortem and a trimmed log bundle for your review.

If you’d like we can set a short 20-minute sync to walk through the timeline and client mitigations. Deeply sorry for the disruption — and thanks for your patience and for surfacing the traces so quickly.

Best regards,
Ben Carter
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
